title: Simple turns and summaries delegated to DeepSeek
description: New in 0.6.0: with delegation on, simple text turns and compaction transcripts of a Claude conversation are sent to the DeepSeek endpoint.
claimed_root_cause: Conversation content crosses to a second provider.

trace.description: User toggle, exposed in Paramètres → Comportement.
Helper built only when delegation is on, the active engine is not DeepSeek and a DeepSeek key exists.
Images never go to the helper; only Jev-verified simple, tool-free turns do.

evidence.description: Turn with images, without helper, or with delegation off stays on the main engine.
Text engines receive a placeholder instead of image data.

reason: Intended, user-consented data flow (default approved by the owner on 2026-10-24) behind an explicit toggle and an existing DeepSeek key; same proxy, TLS and kill-switch. No lower-trust principal gains anything.

title: DPAPI output buffer read through slice::from_raw_parts
description: The static scanner flags the unsafe slice built over the CryptProtectData/CryptUnprotectData output blob as raw-memory misuse.
claimed_root_cause: An unsafe slice over an FFI buffer could read out of bounds or after free.

trace.description: Credential bytes sealed or opened with the current Windows user's DPAPI key.
Slice of cbData bytes over the API-allocated pbData, copied into a Vec.

evidence.description: The slice is only built after a non-zero return and a non-null pbData.
The buffer is copied first, then freed exactly once with LocalFree; no reference outlives it.

reason: The API contract (LocalAlloc'd buffer of exactly cbData bytes owned by the caller) is respected: bounds come from the API, the copy precedes the single free, and failure paths never touch the pointer.

title: Mid-conversation system messages for deferred tools
description: New in 0.6.0: Claude 5+ requests carry role system messages with tool_addition blocks; system content has operator authority.
claimed_root_cause: Untrusted text could reach a system message.

trace.description: Internal tools entries built by context::surface_additions.
Only tool_reference blocks naming a ToolKind are emitted.

evidence.description: Names come from ToolKind::name (static strings); no text block, no user or web content.

reason: The system message carries only references to statically named tools; untrusted data stays in tool_result blocks as the provider requires.

title: Connection warm-up while typing
description: New in 0.6.0: while the draft is non-empty, HEAD requests open TLS connections to the engine, Jev and the delegation helper.
claimed_root_cause: Pre-connections could leak credentials, bypass the VPN kill-switch or the proxy.

trace.description: Throttled to once per 240 s while typing.
Refreshes a near-expiry subscription token, then warms the base URL.
HEAD to an https:// URL through the shared client.

evidence.description: Kill-switch on and no active VPN: no warm-up at all.
Plain HEAD without any authorization header, https only, shared client (proxy and public-only DNS resolver applied).

reason: No secret leaves the process, the same proxy, SSRF resolver and kill-switch apply; the only observable effect is a header-less HEAD to endpoints the next send contacts anyway.

title: Tool dispatcher named exec flagged as code evaluation
description: The scanner's code-eval rule matches the identifier exec in the tool dispatcher.

trace.description: A tool call from the model is parsed into a ToolKind.
match on the ToolKind enum; each arm calls a typed Rust function.

evidence.description: exec is a closed match over an enum; nothing is interpreted or evaluated.

reason: Name collision only. Shell execution is a separate, gated tool (guard classifier + approval), audited on its own.

title: read_file stub resolves a model-supplied path
description: New in 0.6.0: before reading, a re-read check stats the requested path to compare its mtime with the earlier read.
claimed_root_cause: The stat could probe files outside the workspace.

trace.description: Path resolved with guard::resolve_read before any metadata call.

evidence.description: Same sandbox as the real read (workspace or read-only dependency sources, links canonicalized).

reason: The stub path goes through the exact guard of read_file; outside paths fail resolution and fall back to the normal read, which errors.

title: Scanner rule strings and self-test fixture flagged by the scanner
description: HIGH matches for TLS bypass, unsafe deserialization, raw memory, an AWS key and os.system all sit inside the static scanner's own rule table and its self-test fixture.
claimed_root_cause: Disabled TLS, unsafe deserialization, a hardcoded AWS key and command injection in the scanner module.

trace.description: Regex literal describing TLS-bypass code to detect.
Synthetic probe.py written to a temp dir to prove the rules fire.

evidence.description: Detection pattern, not a deserialization call.
Detection pattern for raw memory, not a use of it.
AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP is AWS's documented example key format inside a fixture that is only scanned, never executed.

reason: Every match is data the scanner searches for; the fixture is written to a temp directory and scanned, never run or sent anywhere.

title: Local web index memory growth
description: New in 0.6.0: an inverted index is kept in memory beside the cached pages.
claimed_root_cause: Hostile pages could grow the index without bound.

trace.description: Fetched page chunked (80 chunks, 4000 chars max each) and stored.

evidence.description: 48 MiB text cap plus the 1000-page cap, oldest pages evicted first.

reason: Text is bounded per page and globally; the index is proportional to that bounded text and rebuilt lazily, so a hostile page cannot exhaust memory.
